title: observability-pipeline-debug-notes-zoe-wip
content:
High-level: ongoing flakey drops in traces and intermittent metrics gaps across a subset of services (payments-*, checkout-*). Logs appear intact but many spans are missing or arrive much later (~30m). Hypothesis so far: OTEL collector upstream/backpressure + exporter timeouts + occasional kafka forwarder OOMs during high-cardinality spikes.

Observed timeline / breadcrumbs:
- 2026-02-26 03:14 UTC: Pager alert - trace throughput drop (dashboard: traces-per-minute) for us-west1 region.
- 2026-02-26 03:15 UTC: Metrics gaps noticed on payment-processing service (checkout-metrics route).
- 2026-02-26 03:40 UTC: Partial recovery after restarting otel-collector pod on prod-otel-3.
- 2026-02-26 04:10 UTC: Recurrent gap reported; root cause not yet fixed.

Commands I ran (and outputs / notes):
- kubectl get pods -n observability -o wide
  -> otel-collector-prod-3 had RESTARTS=5 in last 24h, mem usage spiked to ~1.8Gi (limit 2Gi).

- kubectl logs otel-collector-prod-3 -n observability --since=1h | grep -i export
  -> WARN exporter/otlp: connection reset by peer (127.0.0.1:4317)
  -> ERROR queue/consumer: failed to send batch: context deadline exceeded

- kafka-consumer-lag check (internal script): ./scripts/check-kafka-lag.sh metrics-internal
  -> consumer group obs-metrics-forwarder lag peaked at ~150k for partition 3 at 03:10UTC

- curl -sS http://local-forwarder:8080/healthz
  -> {"status":"ok","uptime":"12d"} (superficial healthy)

- grep logs for span-id 0x7a3b... (example trace id: 6f2a1b9b... )
  -> trace spans for request found at app-level logs, but no corresponding spans in Jaeger/Tempo during 03:00-03:30 window.

Error snippets / interesting log lines:
- "WARN exporter/otlp: connection refused: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:4317: connect: connection refused"
- "ERROR queue/consumer: failed to send batch: context deadline exceeded"
- "WARN kafka/producer: buffer full, dropping message"
- "OOMKilled: container "metrics-forwarder" exceeded memory limit"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Backpressure in OTEL collector during a cardinality spike -> exporter timeouts -> queue growth -> eventual drops. Evidence: queue/consumer timeouts + kafka lag spikes.
2) Forwarder resource limits too tight (OOM/CPU throttling) causing intermittent drops. Evidence: OOMKilled on metrics-forwarder and high restart counts.
3) TLS/cert rotation between forwarder and exporter caused transient connection refused errors. Lower priority.
4) Sampling misconfiguration temporarily set too aggressive for payments services during a deployment. Need to verify rollout configs.

Immediate actions taken (and results):
- Increased otel-collector queue settings on prod-otel-3 (pushed config: queue_size 5000 -> 20000) and rolled collector -> slight improvement, but still timeouts under load.
- Temporarily bumped metrics-forwarder memory limit from 2Gi -> 3Gi on prod that handles partition 3 -> restart reduced OOMs for ~90m window.
- Kicked off consumer group rebalance to catch up lag; lag reduced but didn't fully clear (consumer throughput constrained).

Next steps / runbook ops:
- Short term: scale otel-collector replicas in us-west1 by +2, increase exporter timeouts (5s -> 20s) to reduce batch drops. Monitor traces-per-minute and queue depth.
- Mid term: add more robust backpressure handling in the collector config (retry/backoff, persistent buffer to disk) and add cardinality throttling rules for high-card services.
- Mid term: increase capacity for kafka consumers for metrics-forwarder and add autoscaling on consumer group size.
- Follow-up: correlate deployment history (k8s events) against the start of the spike to rule out config rollout.

Questions to ask/notes for follow-up:
- Did anyone push sampling changes on 2026-02-25 -> check PRs and rollout tags (linked PRs below).
- Check kubelet and node-level OOM logs for node that hosted metrics-forwarder (node ip 10.10.3.22).
- Should we enable persistent queue (disk-based) for OTEL collector as a canary on a small subset before global change?

Action items assigned:
- @Amelia: dig into exporter TLS logs and check cert rotation schedule. (linked: Confluence cert-rotation page)
- @Eli: run a controlled high-cardinality load test against prod-otel staging to reproduce queue/timeouts.
- @Zoe (me): implement temporary autoscale for otel-collector and update dashboards to surface queue_depth and exporter_error_rate per collector.

Relevant links / refs:
- Confluence: obs-pipeline-playbook (runbook)
- Jira: OBS-1243 (incident ticket), OBS-1299 (follow-up: persistent-buffer design)
- GitHub: repo/otel-collector#42 (recent config change merged 2026-02-20)

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- The fact that app logs still show spans (and the agent is instrumenting) but those spans never make it to Tempo strongly indicates a transport/queueing issue rather than instrumentation bugs.
- Need to add more granular exporter metrics (per-exporter request latency histogram) so we can know when exporter endpoints are the bottleneck.
- Consider temporary retention of raw spans to S3 for backfill if we can replay into Tempo without breaking topology.

End of notes (move to final postmortem once we confirm root cause).
